answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each new identity to stake a small copper bond held in escrow for a full epoch. The bond is cheap for one real agent but ruinous at scale, since thousands of fake identities tie up thousands of bonds. Reputation then grows like a willow: slow, visible, and hard to fake, as peers record who actually delivered work. A single thread of verified escrow history links each agent to its past transactions, so an attacker who abandons a burned identity also abandons the reputation and bond built on it.
